title: boost-skills conventions (v1)
description: Slot vocabulary referenced by sandermuller/boost-skills vendor skills. Consumers fill this in their CLAUDE.md Project Conventions block. See https://github.com/sandermuller/boost-skills#project-conventions-schema for the published vocabulary.

schema-version.description: Schema-version discriminator. v1 of the boost-skills conventions vocabulary.

jira.description: Jira issue tracker configuration for jira-create / jira-rework / jira-updates skills.

project_key.description: Single Jira project key for issue creation, updates, and rework lookups (e.g. 'HPB').

refuse_other_projects.description: When true, vendor skills refuse to create or edit (mutate) issues outside of jira.project_key. Cross-project linking and mentions remain allowed.

description_format_doc.description: Path to project-owned doc containing Jira description voice rules, CREATE/UPDATE templates, append-merge algorithm. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

github.description: GitHub repository identity. Used by pull-requests, pr-review-feedback, github-issue-updates skills.

owner.description: GitHub owner (user or org) the repo lives under.

default_base_branch.description: Fallback base branch for PR creation when no branch pattern matches. See branches.patterns for per-pattern base resolution.

branches.description: Branch naming patterns + per-pattern base branch resolution. Vendor pull-requests skill scans patterns in declared order; first match wins; no match falls back to github.default_base_branch.

pattern.description: Branch-name template (e.g. 'feature/HPB-XXXX', 'hotfix/HPB-XXXX-{slug}'). Recognized placeholders are vendor-defined.

base.description: Base branch this pattern's PRs target (e.g. 'develop', 'master').

pr.description: Pull-request creation conventions. Used by the pull-requests skill.

title_format.description: Template for PR titles. Recognized placeholders: {issue_key} (full Jira key like 'HPB-1234'), {short_title}.

template_path.description: Path to the PR template read fresh at PR-creation time. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'. Absent file = vendor skips template injection.

gates.description: Pre-PR gates enforced by the pull-requests skill. v1 vocabulary: skill_invoked, shell_command, mcp_tool. Unknown types are rejected by JSONSchema validation.

type.description: Vendor verifies the named skill was invoked in current conversation before allowing PR creation.

skill.description: Skill name to check for prior invocation (e.g. 'codex-review').

window.description: Time window to check for invocation. 'in_session' = anywhere in current conversation. 'since_last_code_change' = since the most recent Edit/Write tool call to a file NOT in boost-core managed agent paths (.ai/, .claude/, .github/skills/, .agents/, or other paths in the boost-core managed .gitignore block).

on_missing.description: Vendor behavior when gate fails. 'stop_and_request' = halt + ask user to run skill. 'warn' = print warning + proceed. 'skip' = silent skip.

type.description: Vendor runs the shell command and checks exit code before allowing PR creation.

expect_exit_code.description: Expected exit code for gate pass. Non-match fails the gate.

type.description: Vendor invokes the named MCP tool; gate passes when tool returns success. Open escape hatch for project-specific policy not covered by skill_invoked / shell_command.

tool.description: MCP tool name in the tool namespace (e.g. 'qa-approval-check').

args.description: Arguments passed to the MCP tool invocation.

testing.description: Testing framework conventions. Used by bug-fixing, test-writing, backend-quality skills.

backend_framework.description: Backend test runner the project uses. Vendor skills invoke the matching runner and follow its conventions.

forbid.description: Test frameworks or category aliases vendor skills must NOT suggest. Atomic framework values: 'dusk', 'panther', 'pest', 'phpunit', 'vitest', 'jest', 'mocha', 'cypress', 'playwright'. Category aliases (expand to atomic sets at vendor runtime): 'js-test-frameworks' = [vitest, jest, mocha, cypress, playwright]; 'browser-test-frameworks' = [cypress, playwright]; 'php-browser-tests' = [dusk, panther]. Adding a new alias is a minor schema bump; removing or redefining an alias is a major bump.

codex.description: Codex invocation configuration. Used by codex-review skill.

invocation_mode.description: Codex invocation path. 'plugin' uses the openai/codex-plugin-cc companion script (default) — supports background queueing, project-aware diff scoping, focus-argument handling, stable file-based result retrieval, /codex:setup auth bootstrapping. 'bare_cli' uses bare `codex` CLI directly, without the companion script — opt-in fallback for environments where the plugin is not installable (e.g. service-account CI runners with no per-user .claude/plugins/ cache).

setup_doc.description: Path to a project-owned doc covering codex install, auth, and any project-specific invocation patterns. Validated for file-existence by `boost doctor --check-conventions`.

spec.description: Spec-file conventions. Used by write-spec, implement-spec, interview skills.

filename_pattern.description: Template for spec filenames. Recognized placeholders: {issue_key} = full Jira key (e.g. 'HPB-1234'); {slug} = URL-safe kebab-case from issue title or feature name (lowercase, alphanumerics + dashes, no consecutive or leading/trailing dashes, recommended cap ~60 chars truncated on word boundary); {date} = ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Empty-placeholder rule: if a placeholder resolves empty (e.g. {issue_key} when no Jira issue), the placeholder AND any single adjacent dash are omitted. Example: 'specs/{issue_key}-{slug}.md' with no issue + 'Set up dark mode' → 'specs/set-up-dark-mode.md' (not 'specs/-set-up-dark-mode.md').

research_docs.description: Paths to project-owned reference docs vendor skills consult during research phase (architecture docs, relationship maps, glossaries). Each path validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

mcp.description: Project-specific MCP server-name mappings. Each value is the tool-namespace segment as it appears between the 'mcp__' prefix and the '__<tool>' suffix in the actual MCP tool name — NOT the package's npm/composer name. Example: tool 'mcp__laravel-boost__database-schema' → slot value 'laravel-boost'; tool 'mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue' → slot value 'mcp-atlassian'. Vendor skills then resolve 'mcp.<slot>' to call the tool: e.g. with `mcp.jira: mcp-atlassian`, vendor invokes `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue` at runtime. NOTE: unlike sibling groups, mcp.* INTENTIONALLY allows arbitrary property names — the vocabulary of service keys (jira, laravel, atlassian, github, etc.) is consumer-defined; closing this to a fixed set would force the schema to enumerate every MCP namespace boost-skills knows about, which doesn't match how MCP works in practice.
